items.article: A new book reveals how the pressures a generation faces have led to a global fertility crisis You don’t have to be a hardline pronatalist like Elon Musk to know that we are in a global fertility crisis . Across nations and continents, birth rates are at record lows. In the UK, the rate has dropped to 1.39 per woman, a decline that is reflected globally. When it comes to declining populations, “only the Black Death in the fourteenth century,” writes Camilla Cavendish in her new book, Generation Maybe , “is comparable to what is happening now.” There are a number of reasons for this, of course, all explored thoroughly by Cavendish, a Financial Times columnist and former policy director for David Cameron’s government who has also probed the problems of the ageing global population in her 2019 book Extra Time . Generation Maybe is thus named because we don’t yet know for sure if millennials and Generation Z are, in fact, having fewer babies, or if they are simply waiting longer to do so: many young people report being undecided, and a combination of factors – including more people attending higher education and increased financial instability – means people are generally settling down later. Similarly, the generational ambivalence or negativity towards starting a family can stem from not wanting to bring children into an unstable or difficult world (I know this to be true among my own friends who have decided against it). items.text: This Is The Truth About My Scott Jennings Dust-Up: Dem Star
items.article: Adam Mockler has revealed what set Scott Jennings off during their viral on-air clash. The 23-year-old commentator who sparked a viral outburst from CNN’s token MAGA host says it should disqualify him from being President Donald Trump’s next press secretary. Adam Mockler tells The Daily Beast Podcast that Scott Jennings lost control during the outburst, which came as part of a desperate defense of Trump’s never-ending war with Iran. “He lost control of himself, and it’s embarrassing,” Mockler said. “I can’t picture him standing up there as the press secretary in these combative environments.” He continued, “I mean, him getting personal with me on the panel is just so below what an experienced anchor should do. I’ve been doing CNN hits for one year. He’s been doing it for a decade. The fact that he lost his s--t due to the Iran war is very indicative of how thin-skinned he is.” Jennings, 48, blew up at Mockler during an April panel on NewsNight with Abby Phillip , after Mockler pressed him on what political concessions the U.S. secured from Iran during Trump’s war, which was still only eight weeks old at the time. Mockler told host Joanna Coles he thought Jennings had gotten “increasingly frustrated” after backing himself into an “indefensible position” by defending a war Trump had initially claimed would be over within five weeks.
